Replace the hardcoded ModuleRegistryPopulator with a dynamic ModuleRegistry implementation that supports runtime module registration, persistent storage of module metadata (default embedded H2, with optional external database support), and validation of module compatibility
The dynamic module registry will use the same module resolution logic as the existing hardcoded registry to ensure no breaking changes to pipeline creation behavior
Implement the module upload REST API using Spring Web MVC with multipart file upload support, following existing Spring Cloud Data Flow REST API naming and response conventions
Implement the CLI module upload command using Spring Shell, reusing the same business logic as the REST endpoint to ensure consistent behavior

Refactor all migrated Spring XD modules to use Spring Cloud Stream 4.x binder APIs instead of legacy Spring XD module abstractions, ensuring they function as valid source modules for streaming pipelines

Maintain backward compatibility for existing module registry bootstrap behavior: modules registered via the new dynamic API take precedence over hardcoded bootstrap modules in case of naming conflicts
assumptions: The Spring Cloud Data Flow admin service codebase is accessible, and the development team has necessary permissions to modify core components like ModuleRegistryPopulator
All legacy Spring XD modules (jms, mail, mongo, mqtt, reactor-ip, stdout) have open-source licenses that permit redistribution in the Spring Cloud Stream Module repository
All required third-party dependencies for the migrated modules (e.g., JMS clients, MongoDB drivers, MQTT client libraries) are available in Maven Central or the project's internal artifact repository
The default embedded H2 database is sufficient for persistent module registry storage in most deployment scenarios, with optional support for external databases if required by enterprise users
Existing Spring Cloud Data Flow integration tests for module registry and pipeline creation are available and can be extended to cover new dynamic registration functionality
Uploaded module jar files follow the standard Spring Cloud Stream module packaging format, including required metadata (module type, name, version, and dependency information) in the jar's manifest
Existing Spring Data Flow security controls (authentication, role-based authorization) will be applied to the new module upload endpoints, so no additional security implementation is required
